newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU raises doubts over BA/American deal.
newsitem.headline: EU raises doubts over BA/American deal.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert says in a letter to the British Department of Trade and Industry that the alliance between British Airways Plc and American Airlines as it stands would strengthen their dominant position on some transatlantic markets, an EU source said on Monday.

Van Miert also warned the DTI not to give early approval to the deal, the source said. The source added that the two airlines would have to sell up to 400 take-off and landing slots to get EU approval.

Van Miert's letter was commenting on a draft decision by Britain's Office of Fair Trading in December to allow the deal to go ahead provided the companies gave up 168 slots at London Heathrow airport. BA has said it is willing to do this provided it gets financial compensation.
In the letter to British Trade Secretary Ian Lang, Van Miert says clearly that the selling of slots is not allowed under EU civil aviation laws.
This opinion is shared by EU Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock, the source said.

The EU's competence to deal with the BA/American alliance has been challenged by both the companies and to some extent the British authorities. But Van Miert left no doubt that if Britain formally approved the December decision, the Commission would start proceedings which could eventually end up in the European Court of Justice. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
